summary: Will Tuladhar-Douglas works in religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Oxford (including Wolfson College, attested 2002), he has served as Director of the Scottish Centre for Himalayan Research and lectured in religion at the University of Aberdeen.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. Educated at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, he taught at McGill (1960–1964) and Yale (1966–1971) before becoming professor at Trinity College, Toronto (1971–1999) and founding director at the University of Toronto (~1976).
Willard J. Peterson is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. Mentored by Denis Twitchett, he has served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1981).

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist who studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University. He was a Junior Fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows (1933–1936) and served on the Harvard faculty from 1940 to 1978.

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1947–1956) and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg (1975). He held posts at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and the University of Heidelberg (~1976–1993).

Willem Caland was a Dutch Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He served as lecturer (1902) and Chair of Sanskrit (1906–1929) at Utrecht University.

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971–1983) and later held posts at Leiden University (~1983–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William Blackstone was educated at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College (~1738–1745). He later held a post at the University of Oxford from approximately 1753 to 1766.

William C. Chittick is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Tehran (~1966–1974), he held posts at Sharif University of Technology, SUNY Albany, and Stony Brook University.

William C. Kirby is a historian and sinologist who studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He held faculty and dean positions at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) and became a dean at Harvard University (~1992).

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College (1801) and founded Serampore College and the Baptist Missionary Society.

William Dwight Whitney was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Williams College, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, and von Roth, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Yale University from 1853 until 1894.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007), served as a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013), and was a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at University College London. He served as President of Shanxi University (1911) and became Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

William Erskine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1787 to 1792.
William Evans Hoyle studied at the University of Manchester from approximately 1872 to 1874 and subsequently at Christ Church from approximately 1874 to 1877.
William Frederic Sinclair was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal School, Armagh. In 1866, he took up a post in the Indian Civil Service.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a sinologist who studied at Indiana University, Bonn, and DLI under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1983 and Halls-Bascom Professor in 1995.
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge (~1921–1925) and later held a post at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1932 to 1969.

William James was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Plymouth College, Harvard's engineering school, and Harvard Medical School. He held successive appointments at Harvard University as lecturer, assistant professor, and professor from 1872 onward.
